title: CostPerToken: LLM API price comparison for developers
excerpt: Every provider of a model, ranked by your monthly bill.
content_html:
Biggest price gaps today

Same model, same workload, a different provider. Each card is today’s cheapest and dearest monthly bill for the sample support bot. Open one to see every route.

Questions

About the prices, the maths and the alerts.

TScost.ts3 rates

function monthly(w, p) {
  const hit = p.cacheRead
    ? w.cached : 0;
  const perCall = (
    w.in * (1 - hit) * p.in +
    w.in * hit * p.cacheRead +
    w.out * p.out) / 1e6;
  return perCall * w.calls;
}

No cache price: every input token pays the full rate.

Is the price comparison free?

Yes. Comparing and alerts cost nothing. If we ever add referral links, each one will be marked, and none will change the ranking.

Where do the prices come from?

Today, from OpenRouter's public model API, checked 27 Nov 2026. Each provider's own pricing page comes next. Every row links its source.

What goes into the monthly bill?

Requests times uncached input, cached input and output tokens, each at its own rate per million. Cache writes, long-context tiers and batch rates are not priced in yet.

What do fp8, fp4 and mxfp4 mean?

The number format a host runs the model in. Lower precision is cheaper and can lower output quality, so every row shows it.

Why is the lowest input price not the cheapest?

Output and cache rates differ too. On DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Wafer charges least for input, yet DeepInfra bills $13.81 less a month.

Can I get the prices as JSON?

A JSON API is coming. People who sign up for price alerts hear first when it opens.
